statements.text: The set of ordered pairs {(a, Science), (a, Culture), (b, History), (c, Literature), (e, History)} expresses the relation from X to Y and is called the relation R.

context.text: Imagine a taxi that charges 4 pounds to start, plus 2 pounds for each kilometre. Let $X=\{1, 2, 3\}$ be the trip lengths in km and $Y=\{6, 8, 10, 12\}$ the possible fares in pounds, with $a\,R\,b$ meaning «$b = 2a + 4$». Write the relation $R$ as a set of ordered pairs (trip length, fare).

statements.text: The expression "read" connects some elements of set X with elements of set Y and determines a relation between X and Y, denoted by the symbol R. It can be represented by an arrow diagram, drawing an arrow from the student to the type of books he reads.

context.text: Suppose three friends, Ali, Mona and Omar, each read some types of books from the school library: Ali reads Science and Culture, Mona reads History, and Omar reads Literature. Here $X$ is the set of friends, $Y$ is the set of book types, and «reads» connects them. Draw this relation as an arrow diagram from each friend to the book types they read, and then as a cartesian diagram.

groups.label: Relations as subsets of X × Y

statements.text: A relation from X to Y, where X and Y are two non-empty sets, connects some or all elements of X with some or all elements of Y.
X × Y is the set of ordered pairs where the first projection in each pair belongs to X and the second projection belongs to Y. Formula: $X\times Y$
If R is a relation from X to Y, then R is a subset of X × Y. Formula: $R\subset X\times Y$
If R is a relation from a set X to X (itself), then R is called a relation on X, and R ⊂ X × X. Formula: $R\subset X\times X$

context.text: Imagine a bakery where two customers, Salma and Ahmed, can each buy bread, cake or biscuits. Let $X=\{\text{Salma}, \text{Ahmed}\}$ and $Y=\{\text{bread}, \text{cake}, \text{biscuits}\}$. Suppose Salma bought bread and cake, and Ahmed bought only biscuits. List every possible pair (customer, item) in $X\times Y$, then decide which of them belong to the relation «bought» and whether this relation is a subset of $X\times Y$.
